why: Grants through FY2025 protect the Delaware River watershed, advocate for clean water and support riverkeepers, baykeepers and Clean Water Fund.
Recent grants (FY2025) to prevent toxic mine and coal pollution, protect freshwater rivers and secure clean drinking water in Great Lakes states.
Mostly health and human-services giving (Ronald McDonald House, veterans, cancer), though it gave $95k each to the Chesapeake Bay Foundation and James River Association.
Colorado environmental policy regranting centered on transportation and climate; its only river work is a Colorado River drought task force, not pollution.
Funds litigation and advocacy against sulfide mining (PolyMet) to protect the Boundary Waters, including WaterLegacy and Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy, through FY2024.
86 grants (FY2024) to Vermont watershed groups for clean water design and implementation, watershed planning, buffer planting and dam removal.
215 mostly environmental grants (FY2025) for stream assessment, coldwater conservation and river restoration with groups like Trout Unlimited and Stream Restoration Inc.
218 grants (FY2025) to restore damaged rivers, protect healthy rivers and secure clean water, including watershed councils and river groups.
165 grants (FY2025) for water quality monitoring, riparian buffers and a fishable, swimmable James River, led by James River Association and Chesapeake Bay Foundation.
Just 4 pass-through NOAA awards (FY2025) to Oregon watershed councils for culvert and fish-passage fixes: habitat work, not pollution, and thin.
